questions.question: Which tag adds images to a webpage?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The <img> tag (short for "image") inserts images into HTML. It's a self-closing tag - no separate closing tag needed!

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The <img> tag (short for "image") inserts images into HTML. It's a self-closing tag - no separate closing tag needed!

questions.question: What does the src attribute specify?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: src stands for source and specifies the file location of the image. It can be a local file path or a web URL.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: src stands for source and specifies the file location of the image. It can be a local file path or a web URL.

questions.question: Which attribute provides text description for screen readers?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The alt attribute (alternative text) provides descriptions for screen readers and displays when images fail to load.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The alt attribute (alternative text) provides descriptions for screen readers and displays when images fail to load.

questions.question: The tag is:
options: An empty tag that needs no attributes

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <img> is a self-closing tag - it doesn't have content between opening and closing tags, so it closes itself with />.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <img> is a self-closing tag - it doesn't have content between opening and closing tags, so it closes itself with />.

questions.question: Good alt text should:
options: Describe the image's content and function
questions.correct_answer: Describe the image's content and function

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Good alt text should describe the image's content and function. Ask: "What information does this image convey?"

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔

questions.question: Images without alt text are problematic because:
options: Screen reader users can't understand them
questions.correct_answer: Screen reader users can't understand them

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Images without alt text are inaccessible to screen reader users, who hear "[image]" with no description of what it shows.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
